title: Sequential Testing, Peeking & Early Stopping
interviewAnswer: Repeatedly checking a fixed-horizon p-value and stopping when significant inflates false positives. Use precommitted horizons or valid sequential methods/alpha-spending when decisions are continuous.
keyPoints: Sequential designs can be valid when planned.
Operational urgency must not silently redefine statistics.
why: Sequential Testing, Peeking & Early Stopping appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
deepDive: Repeatedly checking a fixed-horizon p-value and stopping when significant inflates false positives. Use precommitted horizons or valid sequential methods/alpha-spending when decisions are continuous. Sequential designs can be valid when planned. Operational urgency must not silently redefine statistics. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: A dashboard checked every hour needs sequential methodology rather than “stop at p<0.05.”
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Sequential Testing, Peeking & Early Stopping make?

production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
